title: A security label stored beside the file is not part of the file, so copying the file loses the label
index_line: T-0052 · EXEC · an archive extractor writes members without propagating the internet-origin attribute · c/any-archiver · corroborated
invariant_violated: A protection is assumed to travel with the content it protects. It does not: the 'this came from the internet' marking lives in a side-channel attached to the file record, not in the bytes. Any component that creates a *new* file from old bytes has to decide to carry the marking over — and an extractor that only thinks about content silently drops it.

mechanism.does: the attacker delivers an archive whose container carries the internet-origin marking, as any downloaded file does
the user opens it with the extractor, which creates new filesystem entries for each member
the new entries are created from the members' bytes only; the side-channel marking of the container is not re-applied
the extracted payload now looks locally created, so the shell's 'opened from the internet' protections do not apply to it
the user (or a follow-on document) runs the payload with no warning dialog, in their own context

source.file.name.value: the archive and its members — the trust attribute lives on the container, the payload is one member inside it

guard.format.value: the origin marking (zone identifier / MotW): a *label*, not a format property — this is the guard that gets dropped

sink.file.write.value: the extraction write, which creates a new inode/record and must therefore re-apply every security attribute

encoding.path.value: member names, including nested paths, which decide where the unlabelled file lands

preconditions.expr: the platform attaches a security label to downloaded files and enforces it at open time

check.spec: powershell -c "Get-Item .\\sample.zip | Get-ItemProperty -Name Zone.Identifier" 2>/dev/null || echo 'no ADS label'

preconditions.expr: the extractor creates new files rather than preserving the container's attributes

check.spec: extract a marked archive and query the extracted file's Zone.Identifier; absent = the bug

preconditions.expr: the extracted member can be made executable or auto-loaded (double-click, shortcut, script)

success: the extracted file has no origin marking although the archive that produced it did
double-clicking the extracted payload produces no security warning, while the same bytes downloaded directly would
the container's marking is still present — only the children lost it
failure_like: the extractor copies the marking to every member (the fixed behaviour)
the platform enforces execution policy independently of the marking
false_positive: a payload that runs only because the user disabled the protection — check the setting before claiming the bypass
an archive that was never marked in the first place: nothing was dropped

hazards: the general question is 'which security attributes are not part of the file?' — labels, ACLs, ownership, capabilities, xattrs, quarantine bits; every copier must carry them
this is the macOS quarantine-bit class and the Linux extended-attribute class as well; the Windows variant just has the most users
the archive is a wrapper: the payload never has to be the thing the user opened, which is why content scanning of the container misses it
the fix is in the extractor, not the OS — so a single unpatched archiver reopens the whole class on a patched machine
non_transfers: platforms that carry the origin decision inside the file's own metadata (or sign the payload)
